summary: Bulgaria is now a full Schengen member (air and sea borders from March 2024, land borders from January 2025) and adopted the euro in January 2026: EU and EFTA citizens enter freely, around 60 visa-exempt nationalities get 90 days in any 180 across the whole Schengen Area, and everyone else needs a €90 Schengen short-stay visa.

defaultStayWindow.text: 90 days in any rolling 180-day period, counted across the whole Schengen Area rather than per country. The day you arrive counts as the first day and the day you leave counts as the last. Leaving and coming back does not reset the allowance: on any given day, days already spent anywhere in the area during the preceding 180 still count against the 90.

travelInsurance.text: Schengen visa applicants must hold travel medical insurance covering at least €30,000, valid across the Schengen Area for the whole stay. Visa-exempt visitors are not required to show it, but cover is strongly recommended.

declarations.name: EES — Entry/Exit System (biometric registration)
declarations.submitWindow: At the border on first entry
declarations.text: Non-EU travelers are registered biometrically (fingerprints and photo) in the EU Entry/Exit System at Schengen external borders. There is nothing to submit in advance, but allow extra time on your first entry.

declarations.name: ETIAS — European Travel Information and Authorization System

fee.notes: Free for under-18s and over-70s. Valid 3 years or until passport expiry.

declarations.text: Visa-exempt travelers will need an ETIAS travel authorization to enter the Schengen Area. It is not yet in operation, and no applications are being collected; the EU will announce the start date several months before launch. Check the official EU site for the current status and apply only there.

currencyLimits.text: Cash of €10,000 or more (or the equivalent) must be declared when entering or leaving the EU.

notes: Arriving from outside the EU, the EU's Your Europe portal gives a duty-free allowance of 4 litres of still wine and 16 litres of beer, plus 1 litre of spirits over 22% (or 2 litres of fortified or sparkling wine); 200 cigarettes (or 250 g of tobacco) by air, but Bulgaria applies the lower limit of 40 cigarettes (or 50 g of tobacco) to travellers arriving by land or sea; and other goods worth up to €300, or €430 by air or sea. Under-17s get no alcohol or tobacco allowance.

Between EU countries there is no fixed limit on goods for your own use, but Bulgaria may set guideline quantities for alcohol and tobacco, which cannot be lower than 800 cigarettes or 10 litres of spirits.
The UK Foreign Office says you cannot take meat, milk or products containing them into the EU, with some exceptions such as powdered baby milk and medically required foods.

payments.text: Canada's travel advice says Bulgaria's economy is primarily cash-based, though most businesses also accept major credit cards and ATMs are widely available. The UK Foreign Office says major credit and debit cards are accepted in most banks and hotels.

safety.text: Bulgaria is a safe destination overall. Watch for pickpocketing in Sofia and at busy Black Sea resorts, taxi overcharging (the UK Foreign Office advises official, licensed taxis, and at Sofia airport the official taxi booking office in the arrivals hall), and occasional rough road conditions outside main routes.

bestTimeToVisit.text: No official source we could read gives a best time to visit Bulgaria. The CIA World Factbook describes a temperate climate with cold, damp winters and hot, dry summers.

roadVignette.appliesTo: Vehicles up to 3.5 t and M1 motor caravans, on the whole tolled national road network — not just motorways.

penalty.notes: Compensatory fee a driver caught without a valid e-vignette can pay instead of a fine.

roadVignette.text: Bulgaria's e-vignette is registered to the number plate and checked by camera; nothing goes on the windscreen. New euro prices took effect on August 1, 2026. Buy from bgtoll.bg, the BGTOLL app, staffed desks at the main border crossings, self-service terminals or the agency's listed partners. No extra fee should be added anywhere.

driving.text: Bulgaria is a party to both the 1949 Geneva and the 1968 Vienna Conventions on Road Traffic, so it recognizes an International Driving Permit issued under either. tips.text: Bulgaria is now fully in Schengen. There are no routine checks at land borders with Greece and Romania, and your days in Bulgaria count against the same 90/180 Schengen allowance as France or Germany.

The UK Foreign Office reports unlicensed taxis overcharging passengers from Sofia airport: use the official taxi booking office in the arrivals hall, check the licence sticker and tariffs on the window, and check that the meter is working.

Bulgaria has used the euro since 1 January 2026. The UK Foreign Office says the lev was accepted only until 31 January 2026; Canada's travel advice says outdated leva can be exchanged free of charge at the Bulgarian National Bank.
Once ETIAS becomes mandatory, apply only at the official travel-europe.europa.eu site — unofficial sites charge inflated fees for the €20 authorization.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Bulgaria?
faq.answer: EU, EEA and Swiss citizens enter freely with a passport or ID card. Citizens of around 60 countries — including the US, UK, Canada, Australia and Japan — can visit visa-free for 90 days in any 180-day period across the whole Schengen Area. Everyone else needs a €90 Schengen short-stay visa from a Bulgarian mission.

faq.question: Is Bulgaria in the Schengen Area?
faq.answer: Yes — Bulgaria joined for air and sea borders in March 2024 and for land borders in January 2025. Schengen visas issued by any member state are valid for Bulgaria, and days spent in Bulgaria count against the shared 90/180 allowance.

faq.question: What currency does Bulgaria use?
faq.answer: The euro (EUR). Canada's travel advice says Bulgaria joined the euro area in 2026 and that outdated leva can be exchanged free of charge at the Bulgarian National Bank. It also says the economy is primarily cash-based, though most businesses accept major credit cards.

faq.question: Is ETIAS required to enter Bulgaria?
faq.answer: ETIAS is the EU's travel authorization for visa-exempt visitors. It is not yet in operation, and no applications are being collected; the EU will announce the start date several months before launch. Once mandatory, it will cost €20 (free for under-18s and over-70s) and cover Bulgaria along with the rest of the Schengen Area.

faq.question: How do I stay in Bulgaria longer than 90 days?
faq.answer: Apply for a long-stay (type D) visa at the Bulgarian mission in your country of residence, tied to a purpose such as work, study or retirement, and then convert it to a residence permit in Bulgaria. The Schengen short-stay allowance itself cannot be extended.
